business_summary.text: Park Medi World operates a network of multi-super speciality hospitals across North India, focused on affordable tertiary and quaternary care.

call_points.text: PAT margin expansion of 220 bps YoY was largely due to lower interest outgo after substantial term debt repayment.
Company aims to reach 5,460 bed capacity by March 2028.

guidance.statement: FY27 revenue expected at ₹2,080 Cr, up 24% YoY.
FY27 EBITDA expected at ₹530 Cr, up 25% YoY.
FY27 PAT expected at ₹360 Cr, up 32% YoY.
ARPOB growth guided at 10%-12% annually for the next two years.
Bed capacity to reach 4,740 by FY27-end and 5,740 by FY28.

K P S Wellness Private Limited

operating_notes.text: Total bed capacity reached 3,610 beds as of March 31, 2026, following the addition of 610 beds during FY26.
Total bed capacity reached 3,610 beds as of March 31, 2026.
Agreed to acquire V3 Healthcare Private Limited (The Medicity Hospital, Rudrapur) adding 330 beds across two tranches by April 2030.
IPD volumes were 26,304 patients in Q1FY27, up 16% YoY, and OPD volumes were 2,23,446, up 17% YoY.
High-end specialties contributed approximately 62% of Q1FY27 revenue, up 440 bps YoY.
Capex per bed remains at ₹37 lakh, which management said is the lowest among listed healthcare peers.

Income Tax verification conducted from 12 to 17 Oct 2026 at premises of listed entity, 14 subsidiaries, Chairman Dr. Ajit Gupta, MD Dr. Ankit Gupta, and CFO Rajesh Sharma; no order passed as of 23 Oct 2026.

timeline.summary: Park Medi World incorporates step-down subsidiary Healplus Medical Services Private Limited for healthcare services
Park Medi World submitted audited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and year ended March 31, 2026.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹460.41 Cr, net profit to shareholders ₹70.86 Cr.
Park Medi World reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹1,679 Cr and PAT of ₹274 Cr during its earnings call on May 13, 2026.
Park Medi World appointed cost, internal, and secretarial auditors for FY27.
Park Medi World submitted the Monitoring Agency Report for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, showing ₹7,023.02 Mn utilized out of ₹7,700 Mn IPO proceeds.
Park Medi World entered into a definitive agreement to acquire V3 Healthcare Private Limited, operator of The Medicity Hospital in Rudrapur, for an all-cash consideration of ~₹177 Crore.
Park Medi World announced the divestment of its 55% stake in subsidiary Devina Derma for ₹0.06 crore.
On 4 August 2026, Park Medi World's Q1FY27 earnings call guided FY27 revenue to ₹2,080 Cr (+24%) and PAT to ₹360 Cr (+32%), with bed capacity targeted at 4,740 by FY27-end and 5,740 by FY28.
Income Tax Department concluded verification/search conducted from 12 to 17 October 2026 across premises of the company, 14 subsidiaries, and promoters.

watchlist.response: Management said mature hospitals are growing 18-20% and it expects to overachieve the guidance, without giving a split.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for a split of the 24% revenue growth guidance between ARPOB and occupancy.

watchlist.response: Management said the 7%-7.5% benefit would be spent on equipment and maintenance, not flow to EBITDA, and reiterated a 26%-27% EBITDA margin.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked how much of the CGHS rate hike would flow through to EBITDA from Q2 onwards.

watchlist.response: Management said it is difficult to project a percentage mix and declined to give a target.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for a target for the high-end specialty (CONGO) mix over the next two to three years.

watchlist.response: Management said it is too early to comment, citing the December 2028 deadline.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked about the timeline for reducing promoter shareholding to 75%.
